pick.name: Super Productivity
pick.what: Open-source daily planner with timeboxing, pomodoro/focus mode, time tracking and GitHub/Linear/Jira issue import
pick.why: Pulls your GitHub issues into today's plan, tracks time per task (for services invoicing) and works offline on Windows + Android with no account
pick.free_limits: Fully free; optional sync via its E2E SuperSync, Dropbox or WebDAV

alts.name: Toggl Track (Free)
alts.what: Cloud time tracker with timers, calendar integration and reports
alts.why: Best when a consulting client wants polished timesheet reports; flips the choice for billable services work
alts.free_limits: Free: up to 3 users (teams), manual + live timers, Google/Outlook calendar integration, personal reports; Starter ~$9/user/mo

alts.name: ActivityWatch
alts.what: Automatic local tracker of which apps/sites you use
alts.why: Zero-effort, data stays local; good to audit where the week went; no task planning

candidates.name: Super Productivity
candidates.verdict: PICK: planner + timer + issue import, MIT, Windows + Android

candidates.name: ActivityWatch
candidates.verdict: Passive auto-tracking; may look like monitoring software to company IT

candidates.name: WakaTime
candidates.verdict: Coding-time only; free plan shows just 1 week of dashboard history; AI coding stats are Premium

decision: Super Productivity gives a solo founder one free, offline-capable place to plan the day from GitHub issues and log time, on both laptop and phone. Use Toggl Track instead when a services client needs shareable timesheets. ActivityWatch is optional; check company policy before running a tracker that logs every window.
details: Pairs with GitHub Issues (backlog) and Reclaim (calendar).

verify.note: Super Productivity v19.3.1 released 25 Oct (2026) confirmed on releases page; MIT; reasonable free pick.
